name: Distinguished Business Leader Scholarship (High School)
deadline: April 15 at 5:00 PM ET (year not stated; the page currently reflects the 2025-26 cycle)
apply: Submit the application form, a one-page cover letter on FBLA, business, leadership and community activities, a resume of FBLA and educational achievements, and one recommendation letter from your adviser or a business or community leader.
eligibility: Graduating FBLA High School members who plan to pursue postsecondary education and become actively involved in FBLA Collegiate. Must be dues-paid by March 1 and have reached the Advocate or Capstone level of the Business Achievement Awards program.
notes: Confirm the 2026-27 deadline with FBLA before applying.

provider: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA) and Pearson
name: FBLA x Futures Scholarship
value: $2,000 each to three recipients, paid to the college
deadline: Not stated on the official page; the last cycle notified winners by June 1, 2026
apply: Apply through the application link on FBLA's high school scholarships page when the next cycle opens.
eligibility: Active FBLA members who are high school juniors or seniors (or college undergraduates), age 16 or older, legal U.S. residents, intending to attend an accredited U.S. college or university. Selection weighs leadership, academic commitment and FBLA engagement.
notes: The posted cycle is for students enrolling in 2026-27 or 2027-28; watch for a new cycle.

name: William P. Elrod Memorial Scholarship
deadline: May 1 each year
apply: Log in to the Student Member Site in the TSA Membership System to get the application materials.
eligibility: Current TSA student members.
notes: The official page does not list selection criteria; see the application in the member system.

provider: Technology Student Association (TSA) and National Technical Honor Society
name: NTHS Scholarship for TSA Members
value: Three $1,000 scholarships, awarded at the 2027 National TSA Conference
deadline: Not stated on the official page
apply: Email the completed application with required attachments to general@tsaweb.org; get the form through the TSA Student Member Site.
eligibility: Current members of both TSA and NTHS (National Technical Honor Society).
notes: Requires dual membership in TSA and NTHS.

name: HOSA Scholarships
value: Multiple sponsor scholarships (in 2023, 92 members received $111,500 from 32 sponsors)
deadline: Not stated; the posted page is for the 2024 cycle
apply: Submit the HOSA scholarship application on HOSA's scholarship page when the current cycle opens.
eligibility: Current HOSA members who are high school seniors, postsecondary or collegiate students, or pursuing a certification, planning health care careers.
notes: HOSA has not posted a current-cycle page; amounts and deadlines are not stated.

name: Key Club International Scholarships
value: Multiple donor scholarships (amounts listed in the application portal)
deadline: Annual timeline: opportunities posted November 1, applications due February 1, recipients notified in April
apply: Create an account in Foundant and submit one universal application with a personal statement, one letter of recommendation and an unofficial transcript.
eligibility: Members in good standing of Key Club International (or Circle K International) completing their final year of high school.
notes: Criteria are set by each donor and may differ between scholarships. The 2026-27 opportunities are not posted until November 1.

name: PDK International Scholarships for Educators Rising Members
value: About 100 scholarships a year, from $500 to $4,000 (one-time and renewable)
deadline: 2027-28 applications open in December; the last cycle closed March 1, 2026
apply: Complete one application to be considered for every scholarship you qualify for.
eligibility: Members in good standing of Educators Rising (high school membership is $15 a year, with fee waivers available) who are pursuing a career in education and will be enrolled in higher education in the fall of the application year.
notes: Donors set specific criteria for individual scholarships.

name: Quill and Scroll Student Scholarships in Journalism (Nell, Gallup and Johns awards)
value: Scholarships (amounts not stated on the official page)
deadline: Not stated on the official page
apply: Follow Quill and Scroll's scholarship instructions; Nell and Gallup awards require a national win in a Quill and Scroll contest.
eligibility: Seniors. Edward J. Nell Memorial and George and Ophelia Gallup awards: national winners in the Writing, Visual, Multimedia Contest or the Yearbook Excellence Contest. Richard P. Johns award: all Quill and Scroll senior members. Must attend a college that offers a journalism or communications major.
notes: Amounts and deadlines are not posted.

name: SNHS Student Scholarship and Arepalli-Karumuri Family Grant
value: $1,000 each (two awards)
deadline: The last cycle closed January 31, 2026; the 2027 cycle is not posted
apply: Apply on the online scholarship platform; recommendation letters must arrive by the deadline.
eligibility: Seniors who are current members of an active SNHS chapter with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5. The family grant targets students who excelled in science fair competitions.
notes: Watch for the 2027 cycle, likely in winter.

name: 4-H Youth in Action Awards
value: Four winners each receive a $5,000 scholarship paid to their school, plus media training and paid travel as a national spokesperson
deadline: The 2027 application is closed; the 2028 application opens in January 2027
apply: Submit the Youth in Action application on 4-H.org when it opens.
eligibility: 4-H youth who are making a difference in their communities.
notes: Age and grade limits for the 2028 program are not posted; check that a senior can apply.

name: Eagle Scout of the Year Scholarship
value: $10,000 to the Eagle Scout of the Year; three runner-up scholarships of $2,500
deadline: Nomination window November 1 to March 1 each year; packets must reach your American Legion Department (state) by March 1
apply: Download the nomination form during the window and submit the packet to the American Legion Department in the state where your Scout unit is chartered.
eligibility: Registered active Scouting America members who have earned the Eagle Scout Award and a religious emblem, are at least 15 and enrolled in high school, and either belong to a unit chartered to an American Legion post, auxiliary unit or SAL squadron, or have a parent or grandparent who is a current Legion, SAL or Auxiliary member.
notes: Legion family connection or a Legion-chartered unit is required.

name: Gold Award Scholarship
value: $5,000 to one Gold Award Girl Scout per council and one from USA Girl Scouts Overseas
deadline: The 2026 program ran March 13 to April 14, 2026; 2027 details not posted
apply: Answer four questions about your Gold Award project in video (3 minutes or less) or writing (500 words or fewer), with a headshot and confirmation of Gold Award status.
eligibility: Gold Award Girl Scouts who are high school seniors (or recent graduates) with the final report approved in GoGold within the eligibility window. Past applicants cannot reapply.
notes: Check back in 2027 for the class of 2027 window.

name: Frank L. Weil Memorial Eagle Scout Scholarship
value: Two one-time $5,000 scholarships
deadline: The posted 2024 application accepted postmarks from October 1 to March 31; a current-year application is not posted
apply: Complete the Eagle Scout Scholarship application (fillable PDF) and mail it in the stated window.
eligibility: Registered, active Scouts BSA, Varsity or Venturing members who have earned the Eagle Scout Award, are active synagogue members holding the Ner Tamid or Etz Chaim emblem, and are in their final year of high school.
notes: The Vernon and Arkans scholarships on the same form require financial need; the Weil scholarship does not state a need requirement.

name: Scout of the Year
value: Scholarships at local, state and national levels (amounts not stated on the official page)
deadline: Entry due to a local VFW Post by March 1 (annual)
apply: Submit the entry form, resume, scouting record, community service record and letters of recommendation to one local VFW Post.
eligibility: Registered, active Scouts who have earned the Eagle Scout Award, Girl Scout Gold Award, Venturing Summit Award or Sea Scout Quartermaster Award; maximum age 18 (still eligible if you turn 18 during the nomination year and are in high school at the deadline).
notes: Posts forward winners to the state by April 1 and states to national by May 1.

name: NEHS Scholarships
value: More than $90,000 a year to 30 or more students; at least one $5,000 Dr. William C. Johnson scholarship
deadline: Two rounds for the Class of 2027 (fall and winter); exact dates not posted
apply: Submit a critical analytical essay (850 words maximum) on a Common Reader text plus a 1 to 2 minute video; you may enter one or both cycles.
eligibility: High school seniors who are NEHS student members in a school with an active chapter, planning to attend an accredited two- or four-year college.
notes: Fall cycle text: Accountable by Dashka Slater. Winter cycle text: The Nightingale by Kristin Hannah.

name: Joseph Adams Senior Scholarship
value: $2,000 and $1,000 scholarships
deadline: The 2025-26 deadline was December 9, 2025; 2026-27 not posted
apply: Your chapter sponsor submits one application per chapter for each award.
eligibility: Graduating senior members of SHH who have shown high achievement in Spanish or Portuguese throughout high school.
notes: Only one application per chapter; talk to your SHH sponsor early.

provider: National Council for the Social Studies
name: Rho Kappa Scholarship
value: One $1,500 grant, awarded in May
deadline: The 2027 application opens in Spring 2027 (the 2026 deadline was April 17, 2026)
apply: Your Rho Kappa advisor runs an internal selection and submits one essay (500 words maximum), recommendation letter and application per chapter.
eligibility: Inducted graduating seniors in a Rho Kappa chapter in good standing with a minimum 3.75 cumulative GPA (or equivalent).
notes: The 2026 essay asked about civic engagement and your community service project.

provider: Family, Career and Community Leaders of America (FCCLA)
name: FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application
value: Several scholarships, including the FCCLA Memorial Scholarship ($2,500), three NTHS scholarships ($1,000 each), and hospitality and culinary awards ($500 to $1,000)
deadline: March 1, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET
apply: Log in to the FCCLA Member Portal, open Surveys and Applications, and choose Scholarships to complete one unified application.
eligibility: Active FCCLA members who are graduating high school seniors. Each award adds criteria (for example, the Memorial Scholarship requires plans for a four-year degree; NTHS awards require NTHS membership; the Zwilling Culinary award requires a 3.0 unweighted GPA).
notes: Use FCCLA's scholarship rubric when writing your application.

name: CAP Cadet Academic Scholarships (CadetInvest)
value: Generally $1,000 to $2,500; the Board of Governors Academic Scholarship is $2,500 for two cadets
deadline: 2027 applications projected to open December 15, 2026 and close January 15, 2027 at 12 noon Central
apply: Submit the primary scholarship application and at least one scholarship subevent in Registration Zone (e-Services), with a resume and 1 to 3 recommendation letters; unit and wing commanders must approve by the deadline.
eligibility: Current, active CAP cadets in good standing who have earned the Billy Mitchell Award or higher, are high school seniors or graduates, and are accepted to or have applied to a postsecondary school. Recipients from the prior three years are not eligible.
notes: Some listed scholarships are limited to certain wings or are need-based; the Schroder STEM scholarship requires an essay checked for AI use.

name: AMS First-Year Undergraduate Scholarship
value: $5,000 ($2,500 per year for the freshman and sophomore years)
deadline: January 31, 2027
apply: Apply online at apply.ametsoc.org with an unofficial transcript and one letter of recommendation.
eligibility: High school seniors entering college in fall 2027 who plan to study atmospheric or related oceanic or hydrologic sciences, with a GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

name: ASA Statistics Project Competition (Grades 7 to 12)
value: Grades 10 to 12 division: First $300, Second $200, Third $100 (split among team members); first-place winners also receive TI graphing calculators
deadline: Projects due June 1 each year; winners announced in August
apply: Complete the online entry form and upload the project as a PDF.
eligibility: Students in grades 7 to 12 living in the United States or Canada, individually or in teams of up to four.

name: ASA Data Visualization Poster Competition (Grades K to 12)
value: First $300, Second $200, Third $100 per grade division (split among collaborators)
deadline: April 1 (annual)
apply: Complete the online entry form and upload a high-quality image or PDF of the poster.
eligibility: K to 12 students; entries are judged in grade divisions.
notes: The page states the deadline without a year.

name: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
value: More than 60 scholarships from $2,500 to $20,000
deadline: Closed for now; the application opens in November
apply: Submit one application to be considered for every scholarship you qualify for.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and college students pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree in technical fields that directly support manufacturing, including engineering.
notes: The Foundation offers both merit and need-based scholarships.

name: ASHRAE High School Senior Scholarships
value: Four one-year scholarships of $3,000
deadline: April 1 (annual deadline for all ASHRAE Society Scholarships)
apply: Apply online and send an official transcript, a letter of acceptance from your college, and three signed recommendation letters.
eligibility: High school seniors with a GPA of at least 3.0 (4.0 scale) and/or top 30% class standing, accepted into an engineering, pre-engineering or engineering technology program at a school with an ASHRAE student branch or ABET accreditation, in a course of study preparatory for the HVAC&R profession.
notes: Selection criteria include financial need along with character, leadership, service and potential service to the profession.

name: ASME High School Senior Scholarships
value: Multiple scholarships, including 25 ASME INSPIRE/Charles W.E. Clarke scholarships of $2,000 and $5,000 awards
deadline: March 15 (the 2026-27 application is closed; 2027-28 not yet open)
apply: Apply online when invited; include a first-semester senior transcript, a STEM recommendation, leadership activities and family financial data.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors who will enroll full time in an ABET-accredited (or substantially equivalent) mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology program the fall after graduation.
notes: Listed scholarships consider financial need along with STEM involvement, character and leadership.

name: SEG Scholarships
value: $500 to $10,000 per academic year (96 awards totaling about $276,000 in 2025-26)
deadline: Applications open November 1, 2026 and close March 1
apply: Submit one application through Grantinterface to be considered for all eligible scholarships.
eligibility: High school seniors planning to attend college next year, and college students, with above-average grades who intend to pursue a college curriculum toward a career in applied geophysics.
notes: Some awards are limited by citizenship, residency, field or university.

name: Sphinx Competition (Junior and Senior Divisions)
value: Junior Division (17 and under): $10,000, $5,000, $3,000. Senior Division (18 to 30): $50,000 Robert Frederick Smith Prize, $20,000, $10,000, $5,000 Audience Choice
deadline: October 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET
apply: Apply through the Acceptd portal linked from the Sphinx Competition page.
eligibility: String players (violin, viola, cello, bass); the national competition celebrates Black and Latino string musicians. Junior Division ages 17 and under; Senior Division ages 18 to 30.
notes: Full eligibility and recording requirements are in the Acceptd application. Finals are January 20 to 23, 2027 in Detroit.

name: GMBS Music Scholarship Competition
value: 2026 prizes for three vocal and three instrumental winners: $10,000, $5,000 and $3,000
deadline: The 2026 deadline was April 20, 2026; 2027 dates not posted
apply: Submit the online application with recordings; 10 vocal and 10 instrumental semifinalists compete in person in Clarinda, Iowa at the June festival.
eligibility: High school seniors and college freshmen who intend to make music their future focus.
notes: Semifinalists travel at their own expense.

name: Morton Gould Young Composer Awards
value: Cash prizes (amounts not stated on the official pages)
deadline: The 2026 window was January 6 to February 6, 2026; 2027 dates not posted
apply: Submit the online application and scores; a parent or guardian submits for entrants under 18.
eligibility: Composers of original concert music at least 13 years old and under 30, who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or students on a valid U.S. student visa, and are ASCAP members or not affiliated with another performing rights organization.

name: Senior Brass and Voice Performance Competitions
value: National Winner $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Merit Awards $100 (separately for brass and voice)
deadline: Registration opens November 1, 2026 on Acceptd; video deadline December 2, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. ET
apply: Register and upload a preliminary video on Acceptd; seven finalists per category perform live at the MTNA National Conference (April 2 to 6, 2027, St. Louis).
eligibility: Brass players (trumpet, horn, euphonium, trombone, tuba) and singers ages 15 to 18 on January 1, 2027, entered by a teacher.
notes: Entry fee $150. The teacher must be an active MTNA member or pay a $200 nonmember fee. The Senior piano, strings, woodwinds and composition registration closed September 9, 2026.

name: Stillman Kelley National Instrumental Awards and Thelma Byrum Piano Award
value: $2,000 first, $1,000 second, $750 third, five regional awards of $500; Thelma Byrum Piano Award $750 (for further study)
deadline: March 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website; the Byrum award is given through the Stillman Kelley auditions.
eligibility: Instrumentalists who have not reached their 19th birthday by March 1. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $10. NFMC membership is required before applying.

name: Michael R. Edwards Graduating Senior Performance Award
deadline: May 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors planning to major in music, in the year of the award. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $20.

name: Lynn Freeman Olson Composition Awards
value: $1,500 (High School, grades 10 to 12); $750 (Intermediate)
deadline: March 1, odd-numbered years (2027 is a contest year)
apply: Upload the application and composition on the NFMC website.
eligibility: Composers in grades 10 to 12 (High School level). NFMC Junior Division membership required. This award is exempt from the U.S. citizenship requirement.
notes: Entry fee paid by a private donor. Biennial award.

name: Mary Alice Cox Awards (Cello or Double Bass)
value: $2,500 first, $1,500 second, $1,000 third
deadline: March 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website.
eligibility: Cellists and double bassists who have not reached their 19th birthday by the application deadline. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $20.

name: Wendell Irish Viola Awards
value: $2,000 first, $1,000 second, one $500 award in each of the 5 NFMC regions
deadline: March 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website.
eligibility: Violists who have reached their 12th but not their 19th birthday by the application deadline. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $10.

name: Martha Marcks Mack Junior Vocal Award
value: $1,500 first, $1,000 second, $500 third
deadline: March 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website.
eligibility: Singers in grades 10 to 12 who have not reached their 19th birthday by the application deadline. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $10.

name: Marilyn Caldwell Solo Piano Awards
value: $1,250 first, $750 second
deadline: March 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website.
eligibility: Pianists in grades 10 to 12. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $10.

name: Lana M. Bailey Piano Concerto Awards
value: $1,500 first, $500 second
deadline: May 1 (per NFMC chart updated August 2026)
apply: Upload the application on the NFMC website.
eligibility: High school seniors who have not reached their 19th birthday by May 1. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Entry fee $10.

name: NSE/NPE Senior Scholarship (Traditional Scholarship)
value: One-time $1,000 for postsecondary study
deadline: May 3, 2027 (applications open October 1)
apply: Read the rules and submit the application form and media release on the AATSP Exams site.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors; those who earned NSE or NPE medals in 2025 and 2026 and are registered to take the NSE or NPE in 2027 are strongly encouraged to apply.
notes: Full rules are linked from the official page.

name: Children of Warriors National Presidents' Scholarship
value: $5,000 each; three per geographic division (15 total)
deadline: Due March 1 of each calendar year; the 2027 application is not yet posted (the last cycle was due March 1, 2026)
apply: Complete the online application with an essay, veteran proof of service, transcript and two recommendation letters.
eligibility: Direct descendants of veterans who served during American Legion membership eligibility dates, who have completed 50 hours of community volunteer service in high school, for undergraduate study at an accredited college.
notes: Judging: 30% character and leadership, 30% essay and application, 40% academic achievement. Essays are screened for AI use.

name: Spirit of Youth Scholarship for Junior Members
value: $1,000 per department (state) winner; five division winners receive $5,000 instead
deadline: Due March 1 of each calendar year; 2027 scholarships to be posted in early October
apply: Complete the online application with an essay, transcript and two recommendation letters.
eligibility: High school seniors who are ALA Junior members, with three consecutive prior years of membership and current paid membership, and at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
notes: Girls State participation alone does not make you an ALA member. Essays are screened for AI use.

name: Science Olympiad Founders' Scholarships
value: Five $10,000 college scholarships
deadline: The 2026 application ran February 16 to April 13, 2026; the class of 2027 application is not posted
apply: Submit the online webform answering three questions (1,000 characters maximum each); you must submit it yourself.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors who competed on a registered Division C Science Olympiad team during their senior season.
notes: Funds are paid to your college upon enrollment.

name: NCF-Envirothon International Competition
value: Thousands of dollars in scholarships and awards (amounts not stated)
deadline: Qualify through your state or provincial Envirothon; the 2027 international competition is July 24 to 30, 2027
apply: Compete on a team in your state Envirothon; the first-place team from each state advances to the international competition.
eligibility: High school student teams competing in state, provincial and partner Envirothon programs.
notes: The 2027 current issue is Soil Health Management. Prize details for 2027 are not posted yet.
